title: A script with no phone number can use up the day's demo requests, so real gym owners are turned away
what: The member app's 'Tell my gym' sends a gym name to the same demo-request box the website uses, and for these requests no mobile number is needed at all. That box takes at most 5 requests a day from one network address and 300 a day in all, counted over the last 24 hours. Someone sending made-up gym names from about 60 addresses fills all 300, and from then on every real gym owner who asks for a demo on the website is told they sent too many today. HQ's list also fills with fake gym names that have no number to call.
expected: Fake requests from the member app should never stop a real gym owner from asking for a demo; app requests should have their own limit, kept apart from the website's.
who: gym owners asking for a demo, HQ
how_often: whenever someone sends the requests on purpose
fix_line: Give app requests their own small daily limit apart from the website's demo form, and never let one fill the other
